title: プログラミング言語とコンパイラ
subtitle: Programming Languages and Compiler
keywords: Lexical analysis, Token 2.Parsing, DSL 3.Semantic analysis 4.Expression processing 5.Prefix, Infix, Postfix, AST
educationalGoal: In this course, students will learn how a compiler works. This technology can also be used for analysis and processing of data formats distributed on the network. Students will also come to understand the control flow and data management methods of programming languages and gain a deeper understanding of programming languages by learning the compiler algorithms and their implementation technologies.
advice: In this course, students learn practically how to develop compilers and interpreters through compact examples. The following are the main items: 1) Programming language control structure and data management. 2) String search for text data, HTML, etc. 3) Compiler processing (lexical, syntax, expression, semantic analysis, code generation). 4) Memory management for program execution. 5) Execution environment (byte code, virtual machine, interpreter). 6) Compiler-related tools.
books: Textbooks: Reference books: None Reserved books: None
requiredKnowledge: As students evolve with programming languages, architectures, operating systems, software engineering, and usage, it is important for them to have a broad perspective. Since each process of your compiler may not work the first time, please check the operation yourself and gradually expand and understand the functions. Since this course requires knowledge of algorithms, programming, and operating systems, students should check themselves for weaknesses in those fields.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand principles of a compiler and explain how a compiler works.
Be able to extend the token type and syntax from the analysis sample codes.
Be able to explain the operation of functions necessary for program execution such as stack and heap, and data.
Be able to convert expressions to infix, prefix, postfix notation, or AST.

achievementLevels.ideal: In addition to the standard achievement goal, students should: Be able to understand the nature of a compiler algorithm and create a parser that suits their purpose. Be able to read and extend the source code of compilers for existing programming languages.
achievementLevels.standard: Be able to explain the compiler's processing flow and the characteristics of intermediate products. Be able to extend the problem program based on the sample code to get normal output.

lessons.content: Guidance, Compiler overview, Programming language overview, Python language review
String search: HTML language, natural language search (morpheme analysis, n-gram), use of HTML parser, regular expression
lessons.assignments: Creating a histogram of word frequencies

lessons.content: Lexical analysis: extracting Token, BNF, Syntax diagram, Constant, Identifier, Operator, Comment, Keyword, how to use PyParsing
lessons.assignments: Review: Explaining each system development process.

lessons.content: Lexical analysis (continued): Lexical analysis program, Pretty print, Block level counter
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercise, A small exam or quiz
lessons.assignments: Completing the token extraction program. Report #1

lessons.content: Parsing: Domain Specific Language (DSL), Statement (Declaration, assignment, while, if, return), Function, Block
Expression processing: Prefix/Infix/Postfix Notation, Priority of operator, Delta (Three-way railroad junction) algorithm, Stack machine
lessons.assignments: Create prefix from/to postfix conversion program

lessons.operation: Exercise A small exam or quiz

lessons.content: AST (abstract syntax tree): Add and search nodes, Implement tree structure with lists and dictionaries, Structure visualization
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercise, A small exam or quiz
lessons.assignments: Create the convert program from source to Syntax tree

lessons.content: Semantic analysis, code generation: Conversion method to other languages, Memory allocation, Virtual machine
lessons.assignments: Symbol table creation, cross-reference table creation

lessons.content: Recursive, Re-entrant, Reusable, Reallocation, Frame pointer, Heap, Scope, Buddy algorithm
Optimization, related tools: Optimizer, linker, librarian, compiler- compiler , lint, document generator
Exam and review of previous classes
Commentary for Exam, Self-inspection, Related topics
